newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says can help end UNHCR-Kabul row.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says can help end UNHCR-Kabul row.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday it could help the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) sort out its problems with the ruling Taleban Islamic militia in neighbouring Afghanistan.
The UNHCR said on Wednesday it was suspending most of its relief operations in the Afghan capital Kabul, in protest at what it said were arrests and intimidation of its staff by the Taleban.
"We are sorry to hear that the United Nations has had to suspend its operations," a Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters.
He said Islamabad hoped that talks between the U.N. and the Taleban would remove "these misunderstandings" and help resume the U.N. humanitarian effort.
Asked if Pakistan, which is regarded to be close to the Taleban, could help in the matter, he said: "Well, if the United Nations requests us, certainly we will look into it."
The spokesman said Pakistan, in its discussions with the Taleban in the past, had expressed the view that "everything should be carried out in a spirit of conciliation and understanding".
A UNHCR official said on Wednesday his organisation was putting on hold most of its programmes in Kabul "until the security situation improves".

He said four of the 22 local staff in the UNHCR's main office in Kabul had been arrested, while seven Afghan women employees had been told to stay at home since the Islamic Taleban movement captured Kabul on September 27.
The virtual suspension of UNHCR activities coincided with the start of a vital winter relief programme for Kabul.
The agency said that effective security guarantees are lacking, despite assurances given by the Taleban authorities.
